subject: Hosted API: Canary deployment causing P99 spike — urgent
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@nextgenhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Josh Patel <josh@nextgenhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: production latency — seeing 502s + P99 jump since 08:00

Morning Sean —

We started seeing a big jump in P99 and a handful of 502s across our calls to Redwood Hosted API starting ~08:10 PT. Our dashboard shows P95 at ~430ms (normal 120ms) and P99 at ~2.6s. Error rate rose to ~1.8%. Traffic volume hasn't changed on our end.

This is impacting several real-time workflows. I've attached a short dump (perf-snapshot-1005.json) with sample request IDs. Can you confirm if you rolled anything out this morning?

This is high priority for us — our ops and product teams are on standby. Please advise next steps and ETA for mitigation.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Platform Ops
NextGenHealth

Attachments: perf-snapshot-1005.json (json, 120KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@nextgenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: production latency — seeing 502s + P99 jump since 08:00

Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the snapshot. I'm very sorry for the disruption.

Quick status: I'm escalating to engineering and we'll treat this as an active incident. Marissa and Laura are on the thread. Our initial look shows there was a staged canary for model v2.1 deployed this morning at ~08:00 PT across a subset of hosts. We are validating whether the canary correlates with the spike.

Immediate ask for you: can you paste one of the request IDs from the snapshot (e.g., the 10XX ids) and confirm whether those requests had sequence lengths consistently >1024? That will help triage.

I'll push for a canary pause/rollback if it looks causal and we'll update you within 30 minutes with a mitigation plan. I'll also loop in CS for credits if this causes SLA breach.

—Sean
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: production latency — seeing 502s + P99 jump since 08:00

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Canary deployment: model v2.1-attn-optimized landed in the A cohort at 08:00 PT; traffic split ~10% A / 90% B.
- Correlation: p99 latency jumps line up with canary push window and internal traces show elongated kernel scheduling for requests with long contexts (>1024 tokens).
- Error mode: 502s stem from a downstream timeout when the new quantized execution path hit certain sequence-length + batch-size combos; not a hard OOM but a slow tail that trips the API gateway timeout.

Attachments: perf-snapshot-1005.json (from customer) + internal p99-trace-101.png (screenshot of trace heatmap).

Immediate recommendation: pause canary traffic and route all A cohort traffic to v2.0 (rollback for canary cohort). Steps below (ops):
1) Set canary traffic to 0% for v2.1 in the Canary Control Plane (route rule update).
2) Reconfigure autoscaler target for v2.0 to absorb +10% burst for at least 1 hour.
3) Deploy a mitigated v2.1 build that disables quantized kernel selection for sequences >1024 and run a focused A/B test with synthetic long-context traces.

I'll prepare a short post-mortem after stabilization and suggest hard canary stop criteria for future rollouts (p99 > 2x baseline OR error rate delta > 0.5%).

—Laura
SRE, Serving Runtime

Attachments referenced: p99-trace-101.png

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: ACTION: Pause v2.1 canary + notify customer (NextGenHealth)

Team —

Per Laura's triage, please execute the following immediately:
- Pause the v2.1 canary (set traffic to 0% A cohort) and confirm in the control plane.
- Increase v2.0 capacity ASAP (scale targets + warm instances).
- Post roll: collect host-level traces and upload to Sentry under incident 7842.

Sean: please notify NextGenHealth with rollback ETA and provide a short mitigation timeline. PrIyom, please prepare a goodwill package (credit) we can offer; I want an exec-level acknowledgement prepared.

Runbook: https://docs.redwood.internal/runbooks/canary-rollback
Attachment: rollback-runbook-v3.pdf

—Marissa
Head of Prod Ops

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: production latency — seeing 502s + P99 jump since 08:00

Elena — quick update: our engineering team has paused the v2.1 canary and routed traffic back to the stable v2.0. The rollback is in progress now and estimated to be complete within 15–20 minutes.

What we will do next:
- Monitor your p95/p99 and error rates for the next 2 hours and share live dashboards.
- Run a targeted test on v2.1 with long-context synthetic requests; we will not resume A cohort until root cause gating is green.
- Offer a credit to account for incident impact (PrIyom will propose amount).

I will send another note once we see metrics back to baseline. Very sorry for the disruption and thanks for reporting this quickly — it helped us correlate and act fast.

—Sean

Date: 2026-10-05T20:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-Incident: Root cause & remediation plan (NextGenHealth incident)

Elena/Team —

Final summary: our investigation identified a regression in the v2.1 quantized kernel selection logic that introduced a pathological slow-path for sequences >1024 tokens under certain batching conditions. The canary surfaced the regression within the A cohort and we paused the canary.

Remediation and prevention:
- Fix: disable the problematic kernel selection branch for v2.1 and produce v2.1.1 with explicit long-context handling.
- Canary policy changes: require p99 within 1.5x baseline AND error delta < 0.25% for 30m before increasing traffic beyond 10%.
- Test harness: add long-context synthetic traces to our canary suite and run them across quantized/non-quantized kernels.
- Customer remediation: we will grant a one-time invoice credit (details via PrIyom) and supply a follow-up performance report for the next 2 weeks.

We appreciate your partnership and will coordinate a short walkthrough of the fix and the updated rollout criteria.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Prod Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback-runbook-v3.pdf
